attempts.text:
```json
{"rows": [
{"n": 1, "label": "requested", "why": "\"Keep the game rules in a module the server uses, and cover them with node:test tests\"; the export list and test-only supplied fleets only decide how that module and its tests work."},
{"n": 2, "label": "implied", "why": "Resolving \"miss\", \"hit\", \"sunk\" and \"gameOver\" across shots needs per-game state, and in-memory objects are the minimal way to hold it."},
{"n": 3, "label": "implied", "why": "Separate games identified by a game id would corrupt each other if state sat in a shared module-level registry rather than in each caller's game object."},
{"n": 4, "label": "implied", "why": "POST /api/fire takes caller-supplied row/col, so rejecting out-of-board, non-integer and repeat shots without changing the game is input validation the requested rules need."},
{"n": 5, "label": "implied", "why": "Random placement of a computer fleet on a 10x10 grid can loop forever without bounded retries, which would hang GET /api/new and the tests."},
{"n": 6, "label": "requested", "why": "\"GET / serves...\", \"GET /api/new starts a game\", \"POST /api/fire with JSON...\" and \"the port in the PORT environment variable (default 3000)\"; status codes and validation order decide how these work."},
{"n": 7, "label": "requested", "why": "\"returns JSON with a game id\"; an in-process Map keyed by random UUIDs only decides how game ids and their games are held."},
{"n": 8, "label": "implied", "why": "Testing the requested HTTP API reliably needs isolated server processes per case so tests do not interfere through shared state or ports."},
{"n": 9, "label": "implied", "why": "A single-player game is pointless if fleet positions leak in responses, and parsing unbounded or coerced request bodies would let malformed input break the requested POST /api/fire."},
{"n": 10, "label": "implied", "why": "Whoever starts \"server.js\" needs to see that it is listening and see errors, and the plan does this with a minimal startup line and stderr only."},
{"n": 11, "label": "requested", "why": "\"starts the server on the port in the PORT environment variable (default 3000)\"; reading it once and printing the bound port decides how that works, including for tests."},
{"n": 12, "label": "implied", "why": "The tests that run with `node --test` need a time guard so a hung full game fails visibly instead of stalling the run."},
{"n": 13, "label": "requested", "why": "\"a playable HTML page titled \"Battleship\" where the player fires at a computer-placed fleet on a 10x10 grid\"; cells, outcome marks, status and new game decide how the page is playable."},
{"n": 14, "label": "requested", "why": "\"GET /api/new starts a game\" and \"POST /api/fire ... returns JSON with \"result\"\" are what the page uses for the player to fire, and reporting failed requests is error handling of that page."},
{"n": 15, "label": "implied", "why": "Firing at a hidden computer-placed fleet fails as a game if the page fetches or stores fleet positions."},
{"n": 16, "label": "implied", "why": "Keeping the computer-placed fleet hidden from the player requires that the page's markup does not expose ship data."},
{"n": 17, "label": "implied", "why": "Accessible controls of the requested playable page, including real buttons, labels, a live status and a small-screen layout, are rigour on a requested interface."}
]}
```
